desc:
The string s consists only of the characters '{' and '}'. It is balanced when every '{' can be paired with a later '}' and every '}' with an earlier '{', each brace used in exactly one pair.

In one operation you pick a single position and flip its character, turning '{' into '}' or '}' into '{'. You cannot insert or delete characters.

Return the minimum number of flips that make s balanced, or -1 if it is impossible.

For example, "}{" needs 2 flips (it becomes "{}"), while "{{{" is impossible because its length is odd.
hints: Flipping never changes the length, so what can you say immediately when the length is odd?
First cancel every adjacent {} pair with a stack (or counter), as these braces are already fine. What shape can the leftover string have?

The leftover is always some closing braces followed by some opening braces: }}}...{{{. With a closing and b opening braces left, flip every second closing brace and every second opening brace, which costs ceil(a/2) + ceil(b/2).
editorial: An odd length can never be balanced, so answer -1. Otherwise scan the string with a counter of open braces. On '{' increase it. On '}', if the counter is positive decrease it (a matched pair), else this '}' is unmatched and we count it in a. At the end, the counter holds the unmatched opening braces b.

What remains is }^a {^b. Two adjacent unmatched braces of the same kind can be fixed with one flip: }} becomes {} and {{ becomes {}. If a is odd then b is odd too (the total length is even), and the last } and the first { need one flip each to become { and }. Hence the minimum is ceil(a/2) + ceil(b/2). Time O(n), space O(1).
